remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Mrs. Dewald's apartment, Jan. 1946. . . . No signature." Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Information from Mrs. Dewald: This was one of the group of drawings taken to Stieglitz by Anita Pollitzer in 1916. First O'Keeffe to be sold –– bought by Mrs. Dewald. Title given by Mrs. Dewald." Whitney Archive indicates, "Note: O'Keeffe says done 1916 and in second exh. at '291' 1917." Not among drawings Pollitzer brought Stieglitz 1 January 1916; completed after August move to Texas. Pictured in 1917 New York (291) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 5. O'Keeffe wrote: "The first picture I ever sold was sold from that show [1917 at 291]. It was a black shape with smoke above it, a picture of the early morning train roaring in" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 10). The relationship between the 1916 train series and Stieglitz photographs of similar subject that O'Keeffe knew through *Camera Work* is discussed at length by Sarah Greenough in *Art and Letters* (1987), pp. 276–77, nn. 17, 18. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.title: Train at Night in the Desert

description: A small, geometric black form occupies the center left of the paper. The form gives off layers of black, white, and gray steam. Surrounding the elements is a plain gray background.
title: Train at Night in the Desert
